segments.text: Welcome back to the channel. It's time for another episode of GitHub Trending Today. We've got 30 amazing projects
that are trending today. Let's get started.
Nodecast TV, a self-hosted IPv player that brings live TV, movies, and series straight to your browser. No hassle
required. It connects seamlessly with extreme codes and M3U playlists so you can watch all your favorite channels and content in one place. Fast channel
switching, check. Interactive TV guide, absolutely. Nodecast TV handles massive playlists like a pro. We're talking up
to 7,000 channels without breaking a sweat.
Map CN adds stunning maps to your web apps with just one command setup. Built on Map LiberG, Map CN gives you full
access to mapping features right out of the box. It's all ready to go with sensible defaults that work perfectly for any project. It's theme, so it
automatically adapts to light and dark modes. It lets you add markers and tool tips, plus draw routes and paths on your maps.
Tuxmate, the web-based Linux installer that generates DROP specific shell scripts to bulk install your favorite
apps in minutes with 150 applications across 15 categories from browsers, dev
tools, and media apps to security, VPNs, and gaming. It shows availability for each app on your DRO and gives you clear instructions if an app isn't available.
Need to check your internet speed fast?
Meet Cloudflare speed cli. The command line tool that tests your download and upload interface. It shows you realtime
charts with download upload throughput, idle latency, and loaded latency all in one place. No more guessing, just real
data real quick. Track results, export as JSON, and even script it.
Ever find yourself lost in endless tabs, wasting time on distracting websites?
Say hello to Distracted, the browser extension that blocks those sites and forces you to do many tasks to get back to them. Distracted gives you challenges
like timers, holding a button, or even typing random UU IDs to unlock sites. No more mindless scrolling. It tracks your
visits and success rate so you can see how well you're doing.
Love chess, but want to play it straight from your terminal? Meet Chess Tuili, the simple terminal based chess game
that lets you play two-player locally or even take on a UCI compatible engine.
Want to play online? Chess 2 has liess integration and online multiplayer, so you can challenge friends or opponents
anytime. Plus, there's a helpful in-game menu to guide you through and even custom skins to make it your own.
Racula, the drag and drop rack visualizer that lets you organize your devices right in your browser. Drag and drop your gear, move it around, and see
your real device images instead of those sad gray boxes. And when you're done, export your layout to PNG, PDF, or SVG
for documentation or just to print and stare at. Want to share it? Racula even generates a QR code so you can share your layout with just a scan.
Ever looked at your system and thought, "Why is this even running?" Meet Witter, short for why is this running? It
answers one question and it answers it clearly. Instead of dumping raw output like PS or systemctl, whiter explains the cause. What started this process?
What's keeping it alive? Point it at a process name or even a port and whiter traces everything back to the root in one clean human readable explanation.
Pocket Mocker, the inpage HTTP controller that lets you intercept, modify, and simulate API responses
directly in your browser. No more setting up mock servers or writing endless mock code. With Pocket Mocker, you can control API responses with a
simple visual panel. Tweak timing, force 500 errors, or simulate network latency without ever touching the back end.
Juggling AI accounts? Not anymore. Meet Quotio, your command center for all things AI coding. Whether it's Claude,
Gemini, or OpenAI, Quotio unifies them into one sleek native Mac OS menu bar app. No more switching tabs. Track
quotas, monitor usage, and manage your AI tools in real time. Watch your request traffic and success rates live on a customizable dashboard, and get
notifications when things are running low.
Keeper, the open- source calendar sync tool that brings all your events together in one place. It pulls events
from remotely hosted Ical or ICS links and pushes them to your main calendar so your time slots stay perfectly aligned.
No more double booking or missing important meetings. With Keeper, you can easily aggregate and sync your calendar events across multiple sources. It's
self-hostable. You can tweak it to fit your needs.
Need to automate server backups without the hassle of custom scripts? Meet Back App, the lightweight app that lets you schedule and inspect backups of remote
servers via SSH. At under 50 megabytes, it runs locally or on a dedicated machine, offering a simple web interface
to manage all your backups. No more messing with complicated cron jobs. With back app, you can add multiple remote
servers and create flexible backup profiles.
Dockhand, the efficient Docker management tool that makes handling containers a breeze. With real-time container management, you can start,
stop, restart, and monitor containers instantly. Need to deploy a stack? The visual editor for Docker Compose makes
it super easy. Manage both local and remote Docker hosts, access containers with an interactive shell, and stream logs live, all in one place.
Photos Export, a Mac OS command line tool that lets you export all your data from Apple Photos straight to your file system. It's designed to export
everything from originals to live photos, adjustment data, all in a simple folder hierarchy by year and month. Just
one tool, a deterministic timestamp naming convention, and complete control over your exports.
NV, the self-hosted web interface that lets you stream IPv with ease. No bloat or complicated setup. It's perfect for
anyone who wants a lightweight interface that works across desktop, mobile, and even chcast. With NE TV, you get a live
TV EPG grid guide and even hardware transcoding for smoother playback. Need to search or organize content? N TV lets
you search and resume VOD playback in seconds.
Audio Priority Bar, the Mac OS menu bar app that automatically manages your audio device priorities. Set your
preferred order for speakers, headphones, and mics, and audio priority bar does the rest, switching to the highest priority device as soon as it connects.
It's got separate modes for speakers and headphones, so you can manage each with its own priority list. Want to turn your
photos into interactive 3D scenes? Meet Sharp 3D, the web app that transforms any image into a 3D Gaussian splat model
powered by Apple's Sharp Tech. Sign in with Google Oath to get started. Upload any photo, let it process, and then
you're ready to explore your image in 3D. Use your mouse to rotate, zoom, and pan the scene. It's like you're stepping inside the photo.
Want to know exactly what's happening in your app in real time? Meet FYI, the tool that gives you instant insights,
user feedback, and notifications right when it matters most. Event tracking with just one line of code. track
everything happening in your app. A live dashboard to search, filter, and view activity histograms in real time. A
feedback widget to collect user thoughts right inside your app.
Ever wondered if you could build a Linux distribution in JavaScript? Well, now you can with Ultimate Linux, the micro Linux distro powered by pure JavaScript.
It's a minimal user space written mostly in JavaScript with just a tiny bit of C to enable mounting, but it works with commands like ls, cd, cat, and mkdir.
You can run a Linux-like environment in your browser.
EA key, the autocorrect for Windows that works systemwide. This floating typing assistant uses Flutter and Win32 C++
hooks to bring mobile style autocorrect to any app from Notepad to your browser or even your IDE. EA Key listens to your
keystrokes globally, plus a predictive engine to suggest words from your personalized vocabulary. It even remembers your corrections so you'll
never have to fix the same mistake again.
Ditto, the mini library that transforms any color into a full palette. While most pallet generators just pick random
shades, Dot Tones analyzes the perceptual DNA of popular design systems, the lightness and chroma curves
in OK space and maps your color onto those curves. Whether you're working with Tailwind or something else, Dotes
ensures your color game is consistent and beautiful.
Tired of bouncing between your browser and code? Meet Jira.envim, your Jira task manager inside Neoim. Track active
sprints, query tasks with custom JQL, and update status, all without leaving your editor. Read tasks in markdown, log
time, assign tasks, and even comment right from your workspace. Plus, get integration to keep everything connected.
Two moons is a web- based app that makes learning and practicing music theory way easier. Plus, it can be packaged into a
mobile app using Capacitor, a global piano that's always available, so you can capture inspiration anytime, anywhere. A chord editor that allows you
to build and audition complex chord progressions in both guitar and piano views. The MOA roll, a visual MIDI piano
roll editor that lets you easily create and edit melodies.
Clus watcher, your Kubernetes native 247 on call engineer. It runs as a cron job, constantly monitoring pods for issues
like crash loop backoff or errors. When things go wrong, it dives into the logs, applies hot fixes, and keeps track of
everything in an SQLite database. Need a report? Clus watcher gives you the full rundown. With its own web dashboard, you
can see all the detected errors and fixes in one place.
Git Wt, the git subcommand that makes git work simple and easy to use. With git wt, you can quickly manage multiple work trees without all the complexity.
It streamlines the process, making it fast and efficient for developers to work across different branches. Say goodbye to the headaches of manual
workree management and keep your Git workflow smooth with GitW.
Emoji DB, the higherformance encrypted database engine that uses emoji sequences to secure your data, headers,
and schemas. Built with Go and powered by a Node.js JS SDK. Emoji DB offers militarygrade encryption, automatic
binary downloads, and seamless schema evolution. It's a fun and secure way to handle your database, turning your sensitive data into emoji powered encryption.
YouTube Live TTS, the real time texttospech tool powered by 11 Labs.
Watch chat messages flow in and hear them spoken out loud, thanks to AI powered voices in high quality TTS. With
the modern dashboard, you can configure and monitor everything right from your browser. Smart message cues and anti-PAM protection keep things smooth.
Need a seamless way to back up your Apple photos? With immr, you can easily export your photos to local folders organized by date or sync directly to
images photo servers. Choose from incremental, full, or mirror backup modes and filter by album, media type,
or date. Pause, resume, and even schedule automatic backups, all with smooth menu bar integration.
Level up your terminal UI with Bgraph.
Create highresolution BTOP style Braille graphs right in your terminal. With five vertical levels per cell and smooth gradients, you get that seamless natural
aesthetic you love. Add beautiful filled area graphs, gauges, and time series with just a simple API. Zero line
support check. And with Ratatou integration, it's perfect for widgets, miniigraphs, and more. Deeptutor is
designed to revolutionize your learning by combining AI features to help you master complex topics. Whether you're studying textbooks, research papers, or
technical manuals, get step-by-step solutions, interactive learning visuals, and real-time problem solving. Create
custom quizzes, simulate exams, and practice your way to success. Whether it's research or generating new ideas, DeepTutor has you covered.
